memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now the whole world had one language and a common speech. As people moved eastward, they found a plain in Shinar and settled there. - Gen 11:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter opens with a picture of remarkable unity: "the whole world had one language and a common speech." Everyone could understand one another. There were no barriers of translation, no misunderstandings across cultures. Humanity was united as it had never been since. On the surface, this sounds wonderful - and unity truly is a gift.

But notice the direction they were travelling: "As people moved eastward." All through Genesis, moving east has been the direction of drifting from God - Adam and Eve east of Eden, Cain settling in the land east of Eden. And they "settled" in Shinar, the very region where Babylon would rise. Something is quietly going wrong even in this unity.

Here is a truth worth pausing over: unity itself is not automatically good. It depends entirely on what a people are united around. A crowd can be perfectly united in the wrong direction. Human beings can agree completely with one another and still be moving away from God together.

We often assume that if only people would agree, all would be well. But Scripture asks a deeper question: united around what? The only unity that truly blesses is unity grounded in God's truth - the unity Jesus prayed for among His people (John 17:21), a oneness centred on Him. Before we celebrate agreement, we must ask where the agreement is heading.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are the groups you belong to united around God's truth, or something else?
- Which direction is your life quietly drifting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep me from being united with others in the wrong direction. Ground me in Your truth, and let every agreement in my life be one that draws me closer to You.
Amen.
